::: {#exm-double-plus-power-sequence}
#### The sequence $b_n$, defined recursively

The sequence of @exr-double-plus-power-terms is recursively defined (@def-recursive-sequence) with $n_0 = 0$ and $m = 1$.
Its initial term is $b_0 = 0$, and its recurrence relation (@def-recurrence-relation) is

$$
b_n = 2 b_{n-1} + 2^n
\quad\text{for every integer } n \ge 1.
$$

In Racket, where `(expt 2 n)` is $2^n$, the recurrence relation becomes a recursive function:

```racket
(define (b n)
  (if (= n 0)
      0
      (+ (* 2 (b (- n 1))) (expt 2 n))))
```

`(b 5)` leads to calls of `(b 4)`, `(b 3)`, `(b 2)`, `(b 1)` and `(b 0)` in turn,
and returns 160, as in @sol-double-plus-power-terms.

:::
